items.title: Harvey Jones Interview
items.q: Not Grandy. Yeah. I knew Grandy. He played. All right. Grandy came later. He also played jug.

ctx.x: He was the first one around those all. He was the original Jug Blower. Did you ever encounter, Jasper, did you ever encounter jug bands before 20? Well, yes, I saw the original across the street from the barbershop. I played over there. Well, was it this group or another? It was this group. Not Grandy. Yeah. I knew Grandy. He played. All right. Grandy came later. He also played jug. But I wondered if there were other jug bands before this thing started in Louisville. Now, in Louisville there were several jugs…

That's the only one that I know of is Earl McDonnell. I know several that come up after he did, but I never did pay any attention to them, because they weren't the rich one, and they didn't get no jobs in the first beginning. They never was put out or hired for no fine jobs and things like that. But Earl, he showed the Hippodrome, New York, and all the biggest, finest places you could find. He wasn't hired. And when we came here to Chicago in 20, we was hired by Jack Rees. Jack Rees had a cabaret at Ohio on State…
